compatibility.title: Which Vauxhall Models Use the D16DTH?
compatibility.intro: The D16DTH is the PSA-GM co-developed 1.6-litre diesel that replaced the older 1.9 and 2.0 CDTi units across Vauxhall's range. It was fitted to Astra K, Insignia A and B, Mokka, Meriva, Zafira, and Grandland X. With 210 replacement enquiries through our marketplace in 2025 , it's one of Vauxhall's most-requested diesel engines.

failures.title: Vauxhall D16DTH Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing chain stretch and tensioner wear - all variants, 60,000-120,000 miles
items.onset: 60,000-120,000 miles. The D16DTH timing chain system is a documented weak point - chain stretch and tensioner wear are among the most common reasons owners seek replacement engines. Early warning signs include a rattling noise on cold start, poor correlation between crank and cam sensors (P0016 code), and eventually engine management lights . If ignored, the chain can skip, leading to catastrophic valve/piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, chain replacement costs £800-£1,500. However, if the chain has jumped timing and bent valves, a full replacement engine is the only viable route - and used units without documented chain history carry the same risk all over again. → Read our full timing chain failure guide

items.title: Injector failure - all variants, 70,000-120,000 miles
items.onset: 70,000-120,000 miles. Injector failure is common on the D16DTH, presenting as poor fuel economy, unburned fuel smell from the exhaust, rough idle, and in severe cases, fuel dilution of the engine oil . When an injector fails open or leaks, unburned diesel can seep past piston rings and contaminate the oil - a condition that rapidly degrades lubricant quality and can cause serious engine damage.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector replacement typically costs £300-£800 per injector; all four should be replaced together when one fails . If the issue is caught early before oil contamination has caused bottom-end damage, replacement is straightforward. If oil dilution has led to bearing wear, a replacement engine becomes the more economical choice. → Read our full fuel injector failure guide

items.title: Oil pump wear and low oil pressure - 80,000-120,000 miles
items.onset: 80,000-120,000 miles. Low oil pressure warnings on the D16DTH are not limited to the 2.0-litre CDTi's well-known oil pickup seal issue. D16DTH owners report persistent "Oil pressure low - turn vehicle off" warnings, even after oil changes and sensor replacements. In many cases, the oil pump itself has worn internal plastic components, causing pressure to drop at hot idle (as low as 8 psi, when 30 psi is expected) and triggering limp mode with a P06DD code .
items.repairVsReplace: Replacement of the oil pump costs approximately £500-£1,000, but the job is labour-intensive (requiring sump removal or gearbox-out access). If the engine has been run with low oil pressure for any length of time, bottom-end bearing damage may have occurred - in which case a replacement engine is the safer long-term choice .

failures.goodYearsLine: The later D16DTH (Euro 6d-TEMP) engines in Insignia B and Astra K (2018-2020) feature incremental revisions to the chain tensioner and oil pump design, with fewer reported failures than earlier B16DTH units .

variants.title: D16DTH Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: The D16DTH is one of two 1.6 CDTi designations used by Vauxhall; the earlier B16DTH (non-AdBlue) and the later D16DTH (AdBlue-equipped) are closely related but have different emissions hardware and ECU calibrations. The distinction matters when buying a replacement. - Fitted to: Vauxhall Astra K (2016-2020), Insignia B (2018-2020), Grandland X (2017-2020) - Key technical difference: Euro 6d-TEMP emissions standard with AdBlue (Selective Catalytic Reduction) system - the AdBlue tank and injector are added to the exhaust system; ECU calibration is specific for AdBlue management - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern (timing chain, injectors, oil pump). The AdBlue system itself adds an additional failure point - AdBlue injector crystallisation and NOx sensor failures are reported, but these are emissions-system issues, not engine-internal failures - Interchange note: A D16DTH can be used to replace a B16DTH, but the AdBlue system must be retained and the ECU reprogrammed accordingly. The reverse (B16DTH replacing D16DTH) is NOT possible without a full emissions system delete, which is illegal for UK road use - Fitted to: Vauxhall Astra J (2013-2015), Astra K (2015-2016), Insignia A (2015-2017), Mokka X (2015-2019), Meriva B (2013-2017), Zafira C (2013-2019) - Key technical difference: Euro 6b emissions standard without AdBlue - simpler emissions system with only EGR and DPF (no SCR/AdBlue) - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern. Some early B16DTH units (2013-2015) reportedly suffer higher timing chain failure rates than later revisions - Interchange note: Can be replaced by a D16DTH with the AdBlue system fitted and ECU recalibration. If you're buying a used engine for a B16DTH vehicle, a D16DTH is acceptable - but confirm the supplier's compatibility sheet first The engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the front of the cylinder block, visible above the exhaust manifold. It also appears on the V5C registration document (engine number - the prefix letters indicate the code). buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement D16DTH - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used D16DTH can be a cost-effective option for an Astra or Insignia with a sub-£3,000 market value, but ONLY buy with documented timing chain history - ideally a written record of replacement within the last 20,000-30,000 miles. Without this, a used D16DTH is a gamble. Also confirm whether the donor was a B16DTH or D16DTH and whether the emissions system (AdBlue / non-AdBlue) matches your vehicle. Link: used engine guide

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the recommended option for most D16DTH replacements. A proper reconditioner will strip the engine, fit new timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets, piston rings, injectors, and all seals and gaskets - effectively resetting the engine to zero. With a 12-24 month warranty, it eliminates the "will it fail next week?" risk that hangs over used units. The £2,200-£3,200 supply cost is the sweet spot for value. Link: reconditioned engine guide

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for a well-maintained Astra or Insignia that the owner wants to keep long-term. Expect £2,800-£4,000 for a quality rebuild. The main advantage over a reconditioned unit is that every component is individually inspected and, where necessary, upgraded - particularly the oil pump and chain tensioner. This is the option for high-mileage taxis or commercial vehicles where engine failure means lost income. Link: rebuilt engine guide

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Fitting through the EnginesMarket network gives you a single point of contact for supply and installation, backed by a warranty that protects both parts and labour. The D16DTH's timing chain and oil pump jobs both require precision fitting - a warranty that covers both components is essential for peace of mind. Link: supply and fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: D16DTH-equipped Astras and Insignias in the UK typically sit in the £2,500-£8,000 value range. At the lower end of that band, a £2,200 reconditioned engine plus £400-£700 fitting is a borderline investment - the replacement cost can reach 60-80% of the vehicle's value. For a £2,500 Astra J, the honest advice is to evaluate scrap value first. For higher-value examples (Insignia B, Astra K), the D16DTH's service life makes replacement a viable decision.

items.question: What is the most common failure on a Vauxhall D16DTH?
items.answer: Timing chain stretch and tensioner wear is the most frequent cause of D16DTH replacement. The chain stretches over time, especially if oil changes are missed, and the tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure. A rattle on cold start is the early warning - ignoring it can lead to chain skip and catastrophic valve/piston contact. Also common: injector failure causing oil dilution, and oil pump wear causing low oil pressure warnings. → Read the full timing chain guide
bullets: Prevention: 6,000-8,000-mile oil changes with the correct GM-spec oil
Repair: chain replacement costs £800-£1,500 if caught early

items.question: What is the difference between B16DTH and D16DTH?
items.answer: The B16DTH is the earlier non-AdBlue version (Euro 6b, 2013-2017), while the D16DTH is the later AdBlue-equipped version (Euro 6d-TEMP, 2016-2020). The core engine block and internals are the same, but the D16DTH has an AdBlue injection system and different ECU calibration. A D16DTH can replace a B16DTH with the AdBlue system fitted and ECU reprogrammed; the reverse is not possible without removing the AdBlue system, which is illegal for UK road use. → Read the sub-code guide above

items.question: Can the D16DTH be swapped with the B16DTH?
items.answer: Yes, but only one direction. A D16DTH can be used as a replacement for a B16DTH vehicle - the engine fits mechanically, and you retain the existing AdBlue system (if fitted) or add it (if not). The B16DTH cannot replace a D16DTH because the AdBlue system in the D16DTH vehicle requires the specific ECU calibration and emissions hardware that the B16DTH lacks. Always confirm with your supplier before purchasing. → Discuss your options with a specialist

items.question: Is the D16DTH a reliable engine?
items.answer: The D16DTH (and its B16DTH sibling) is reasonably reliable when properly maintained, but it has three documented weaknesses: timing chain stretch (the most common replacement trigger), injector failure causing oil dilution, and oil pump wear causing low oil pressure. Regular maintenance (6,000-8,000-mile oil changes with GM-spec oil) is essential - many examples exceed 120,000-150,000 miles with no major issues, particularly the later Euro 6d-TEMP units. → Get a D16DTH quote ---
